title: st.tabs collapses into a stacked column after certain session-state interactions on 1.59.0 (works on 1.58.x)
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

st.tabs([...]) renders correctly on the first page load, but after a chain of nested widget interactions (in our case: submit a form → click a computation button → select a CSV from the training-library st.selectbox inside a nested expander) the tab widget flattens on the next rerun: all with tab_X: block contents render as a single scrollable column with no tab bar. Downgrading to streamlit<1.59 (latest 1.58.x) restores the tab widget with no other code changes.

Broken: streamlit==1.59.0 (released 2026-07-06).
Working: streamlit<1.59 (latest 1.58.x).

Source
https://github.com/Fodera-Laboratory/PEARL-app — pinned to streamlit<1.59 in requirements.txt for the moment.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python

```

### Steps To Reproduce

Reproduction (against our app)

Open https://pearl-app.streamlit.app/ — 10 tabs render correctly.
In the 📂 Linescan files tab, upload a linescan .txt file.
In the 📊 PLS regression unmixing tab, click ▶ Apply PLS Model.
In the 📐 CLS unmixing tab, click ▶ Run CLS.
In the same tab, expand Water content — response factor method → click ▶ Build response curve.
Scroll to the Pure-water test section, select a spectrum from the training-library dropdown.
On the next rerun, the tab widget disappears — all 10 tab contents are rendered as sequential sections in a single column.
Reloading the page fully restores the tab widget.

### Expected Behavior

Expected behavior

st.tabs() should render as a tab widget across all reruns, regardless of session-state activity elsewhere in the script.


### Current Behavior

Diagnostic signals:
No JavaScript errors in browser DevTools console.
No Python exceptions in the Streamlit Cloud runtime log.
The only warning present is check_session_state_rules for widgets created with both value= and key= where the key's slot is pre-seeded via st.session_state.setdefault(...). We refactored those to remove value= / index= in favour of pure setdefault seeding; the warning went away but the tab collapse persisted.

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.59.0 (broken) → downgraded to 1.58.x (fixed)
- Python version: 3.14 (Streamlit Community Cloud current default)
- Operating System: macOS 26.5.1 (25F80)
- Browser: Chrome and Safari — both affected - Repro also observed in an incognito window (rules out client-side state)



### Additional Information

_No response_

comments.body:
**If this issue affects you, please react with a 👍 (thumbs up emoji) to the initial post.**

Your feedback helps us prioritize which bugs to investigate and address first.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-15893)

This is a **frontend regression introduced in 1.59.0**: `st.tabs` renders correctly on first load, but after a rerun triggered by nested widget interactions the tab bar disappears and all tab panels render stacked vertically as a single scrollable column (a full page reload temporarily restores the tab widget). In 1.59.0 the `st.tabs` frontend was rewritten from BaseWeb's `tabs-motion` to `react-aria-components` (see `frontend/lib/src/components/elements/Tabs/Tabs.tsx`). Inactive tab panels are now hidden **only** via the CSS rule in `StyledTabPanel` — `&[inert] { display: none }` — which relies on React Aria applying the `inert` attribute to the non-selected, force-mounted `<TabPanel>`s. If that `inert` attribute isn't applied after a rerun/remount (the frontend still pins React 18, which lacks first-class `inert` support), every force-mounted panel becomes visible and stacks while the tab bar/selection breaks — exactly the reported symptom. The likely trigger is the panel force-mount + selection reconciliation path interacting badly with a rerun/remount during the described session-state chain.

### Related Issues

- [#15892](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/15892) — *"st.tabs: widget rerun inside a tab renders all tabs' content stacked below the page (regression in 1.59.0)"*. Almost certainly the **same bug**: same version, same stacked-column-with-no-tab-bar symptom, and the same trigger (a widget rerun inside a tab). It includes a minimal repro and notes the `[data-baseweb="tab-panel"]` elements present in 1.58.0 are gone in 1.59.0, corroborating the RAC rewrite as the cause. This issue (#15893) is very likely a duplicate.
- [#8239](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8239) — *"st.tabs & st.expander - Improve handling of frontend state/mount"*. Related because this regression surfaces when tabs are re-rendered/remounted during reruns, which is exactly the frontend mount/state behavior tracked there.
- [#11344](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11344) — *"Custom components rendered in non-active tabs rendered with height of 0"*. A related (but distinct) tab-panel rendering bug involving the visibility/sizing of non-active tab panels.

## Update

This will be fixed in the patch 1.59.1 that we will release today
